name: 24532-random1k1k-70b-8gpu
hardware: 8x H100 80GB HBM3, one a3 node (--gres=gpu:8), driver 570.195.03.
parallelism: TP=8, PP=1, DP=1 -- one node, all eight cards.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=256, bounded at 1024 requests with 10% warmup and 10% cooldown, leaving ~820 counted.
workload: synthetic_text, single turn, fixed lengths, no shared prefix -- 1000 prompt tokens in and exactly 1000 tokens out.
purpose: A 70B-scale writing assistant generating long-form drafts for 256 concurrent users on one eight-GPU node.
launch:
model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct
tensor-parallel-size: 8
dtype: bfloat16

# 2048 rather than the 2000 a 1000-in / 1000-out shape needs: the prompt is rendered through
# the chat template, so the engine's own prompt_token_ids run a handful above the 1000 the
# dataset declares, and an exactly-fitting window overflows.
max-model-len: 2048

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.95
max-num-seqs: 256

# PINNED: left unset this falls through to the SchedulerConfig default of 2048 and quietly
# becomes a different experiment.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

enable-prefix-caching: false

# QUOTED from the source's own benchmark command (`--load-format=dummy`). Weight VALUES do not
# enter this measurement -- every tensor shape, the layer count, the KV pool, the batch
# composition and the number of forward steps are unchanged, and guidellm sets `ignore_eos` so
# all 1024 requests still return exactly 1000 output tokens. What it removes is ~570 s of
# safetensors reading (30 shards x ~19 s) at the front of EVERY run, which on its own was enough
# to keep this item from finishing a run.
load-format: dummy
